answer: A shared purse can back many keys if admission is a one-shot deposit. Each applicant gets a walnut crate that may shoulder only one live key. That key meets three rangers at a summit post, 104 minutes apart, skipping kin. Each ranger holds 17 minutes for a live echo, then records ripple_i = sha3_256(crate_id||ranger_pk||height||i). Lock is 24 POA for 5 epochs; each post costs 0.29 POA. Peers replay occupancy, spacing, and echoes. A crate shouldering two keys, a missed summit post, or a pre-recorded ripple mark slashes 31 percent to the spotting ranger and benches the key 6 epochs.
